extracted.intended_audience: writers and authors looking for an online critique community, beta readers, and peer-editing tools
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating a single online writing community (Scribophile) for use as a place to post work, get critiques, find beta readers, and access educational resources. The page is a product-style review describing features, strengths, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma-based participation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Their karma system means you’ve got to read and contribute to the writing community before you can post your own work. You’ll earn karma by providing critiques to other writers; once you earn enough (the equivalent of 2 or 3 critiques) you’ll be able to post your own writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This system ensures participation and drives you to be a beta reader before you can ask for your own beta readers. Consider this a quality-control mechanism: it encourages reciprocal critique and prevents drive-by posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission metadata (word count, genre, context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile provides details like word count, genre, and more to help you know what you’re looking at when finding work to critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these metadata fields to select appropriate pieces to critique or to find peers working in the same length/genre. Clear metadata helps reviewers set expectations and avoid mismatched feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized groups for focused critique
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many groups subdividing users into specialized focus areas (genre-specific fiction groups, article and blog writing groups, nuanced groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joining genre- or topic-specific groups keeps conversation focused and avoids the noise of large, general forums. Examples: 'The Brutal Butchers' for brutally honest critique, 'Self-Pubbed' for self-publishing advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forums and threaded discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scribophile forums are where all the group activity takes place; forums are grouped around writing, publishing, new members, and book discussions. Dive into any category and you’ll find lively conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forums are useful for asking context-specific questions (e.g., about a single sentence) and for getting multiple perspectives. Active threads indicate community engagement; use them to solicit informal feedback and community advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors tab & visibility of power users
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authors tab highlights recent activity from other users and shows writers’ workshop pieces that are published, making it easy to find 'power users' and read their content/critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newer users should read accomplished users’ posts and critiques to learn standards and modeling of good feedback before offering critiques or posting their own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-sponsored contests
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile groups sponsor writing contests as a way to get to know more writers and get some of your work out there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contests can provide exposure, motivate writing, and offer structured critique opportunities. Use contests to test work in front of a wider audience and possibly gain recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational resources: Academy and blog
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scribophile Academy is a collection of user-generated content about different aspects of writing and publishing; the blog contains articles and guest posts (the blog is thinner but contains useful content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the Academy as a hub for learning critique technique and craft. The blog can be supplemental reading; subscribe to catch useful articles but don’t rely on it as the primary resource given its limited volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta reader access via critique system
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile’s system for connecting content with critiques is a close substitute for hard-to-find beta readers and helps refine your work section by section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the critique exchange mechanism to iteratively improve sections of a manuscript. Expect exchange-based reciprocity; the karma system facilitates finding reliable beta readers through demonstrated participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashboard navigation and discovery features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dashboard navigation includes nine separate pages/tabs (Home, Writing, Authors, Groups, Forums, etc.) with a Home tab that pulls together new posts; the Favorites section helps surface new posts from favorite users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear dashboard aids discovery and reduces overwhelm. Use Favorites to track trusted reviewers and the Home feed to stay current with community activity. Be aware the volume can be overwhelming at first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing model and premium features
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile offers access to all their features for free; the paid plan is $65/year and gives premium features like the option to post as many works for critique at a time as you’d like and more ways to 'spotlight' your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most major features are available free, so premium is optional. Consider premium if you need to post multiple works simultaneously or want greater visibility via spotlighting; evaluate value vs. cost based on your posting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scratchpad / private notes for relationship building
rubrics_metrics.description: The scratchpad is a way to write any other user a quick note; it’s a great way to develop personal relationships with other writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scratchpad/private notes to follow up on critiques, ask clarifying questions, or build critique partnerships. Personal outreach can convert one-off critiques into ongoing beta-reader relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to read existing comments before critiquing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you access a posted story, you can review the comments other users leave; that is always useful before you critique other work to avoid repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading existing feedback helps you add unique value and avoid redundant comments. It also helps you gauge what the author has already received and what issues remain unaddressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform as a holistic hub (critique + publishing discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile is part critique and editing hub and part writing and publishing forum, making it versatile for discussing writing, publishing, and editing while developing your story through peer editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Scribophile not only for craft critique but also to learn about publishing processes, marketing, and the writer’s life. The combined scope makes it useful at many stages of the writing and publishing journey.
